name: Jeff Crank

summary.text: Jeff Crank is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 5th Congressional District, seeking a second term.
He was born in Pueblo, Colorado, in 1967 and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Colorado State University in 1990.

His career includes serving as a staffer for former Rep. Joel Hefley, running a political consulting firm, hosting a talk radio show in Colorado Springs, and serving as Colorado state director for Americans for Prosperity.

experience.text: U.S. House of Representatives, Colorado's 5th District, 2025-present.
Member, House Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittee on Energy and Mineral Resources; Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries), appointed January 22, 2025.
Staffer for Rep. Joel Hefley; Colorado state director, Americans for Prosperity; radio talk show host, Colorado Springs.

H.J.Res. 72, disapproving the national emergency used to impose tariffs on Canada
record.detail: Voted Nay (against ending the tariff emergency). Passed 219-211 over his opposition.

record.title: Amodei/Maloy amendment mandating sale of public lands in Nevada and Utah (House Natural Resources Committee markup of reconciliation bill)
record.detail: Voted Yea. He also voted Nay on a competing Neguse amendment that would have prohibited the land sales.

Public Lands Access Restoration Act (PLARA), H.R. 7979
record.detail: Sponsored legislation to expand motorized-vehicle access to public lands; still in subcommittee as of mid-2026.

record.title: Quad Space Act
record.detail: Introduced with Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO). The bill directs the Secretary of Defense to lead discussions with Australia, India and Japan on cooperation on space best practices, space situational awareness and space industrial policy.

record.title: H.R. 1834, Breaking the Gridlock Act (extension of enhanced ACA premium tax credits), passage
record.detail: Voted Nay. The bill extends the enhanced premium tax credit under Internal Revenue Code section 36B through 2028; it passed the House 230-196.

positions.source_title: Rep. Jeff Crank's first term voting record highlights
positions.quote: Amodei/Maloy introduced amendment mandating the selling of public lands, heard by the House Natural Resources Committee – May 6, 2025 Crank voted ‘Yea.’ Neguse introduced amendment to prohibit selling of public lands...Crank voted ‘Nay.’
positions.note: Contradicts a stated position: the same article reports Crank told Colorado Public Radio in June 2025 that he opposed selling public lands. Votes are weighted above statements under this guide’s rules.

research_notes: Crank's public-lands record is contradictory: he voted for the May 2025 committee amendment to mandate public land sales and against the competing amendment to block sales, but separately told Colorado Public Radio in June 2025 that he opposed selling public lands. Per protocol, the recorded votes (strongest source type) were used for the coded position; a reviewer may want to note the contradiction in the published guide. Could not verify the Pikes Peak Bulletin's committee-vote claims against an official Natural Resources Committee roll call document (committee markup votes are not posted on clerk.house.gov); treated the outlet's direct reporting as reliable per protocol's allowance for local news coverage. Second pass 2026-10-14: added health-coverage, clean-energy-shift and challenge-federal-policies from the Colorado Sun's Oct. 7, 2026 CD5 issue guide, and immigration-notify-ice from the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 CD5 candidate Q&A. Build review 2026-10-14: removed an inferred fentanyl-penalties position based on a border-security quote, which does not address sentencing.
